title: Introduction to Functions
concept: Functions are reusable named blocks of code that take inputs (parameters) and produce outputs (return values).
why: Functions are the primary way to organize and reuse code. They let you write logic once and call it many times.
tips: Every parameter needs a type annotation: `(x: Int, y: Float64)`
If you declare `-> Int`, the function MUST return an Int
Define functions BEFORE you call them (or at the top of the file)
common_mistakes: Forgetting the return type (`-> Int`) and then trying to return a value
Writing `fn my_func { }` without parentheses — must have `()`
Calling a function before defining it — define first, call later
